name: Jin Xiangyu
current_role: Founder, Chairman & President, Gaojin Group (Goldkinn Foods), Suining/Chengdu, Sichuan
profile: Jin Xiangyu (金翔宇) founded Sichuan Gaojin Food (Goldkinn) in 1996 in Suining, building a pork slaughtering, processing, cold-chain and distribution business that took Sichuan Gaojin Food public in Shenzhen (002143). The Gaojin Group remains a large Sichuan private enterprise in meat products, which he still chairs.
interesting_fact: Gaojin Group was ranked 26th on a 2021 Sichuan Top 100 Private Enterprises list and lists exports of its pork products to Russia, Kyrgyzstan, South Korea and Singapore.
deep_cut_fact: Besides running Gaojin, he is listed as a Director of the World Meat Association and Vice President of the China Meat Association, and was a deputy to the 13th Sichuan Provincial People's Congress.
notes: Low English-language profile; only the company website covers him. The company site publishes no email, just a Group Marketing Center phone line (400-008-0303). Approach in Chinese through the company would be best.

name: Renu Sud Karnad
current_role: Non-Executive (Non-Independent) Director, HDFC Bank; Chairperson, GlaxoSmithKline Pharmaceuticals Ltd and PayU Payments
profile: Renu Sud Karnad joined HDFC Ltd in 1978, joined its board in 2000 and was Managing Director from 2010 until HDFC's merger with HDFC Bank in July 2023. Over about 41 years in Indian mortgage finance she built HDFC's retail lending network. She now sits on the HDFC Bank board and chairs GSK Pharmaceuticals India and PayU Payments.
interesting_fact: She has appeared on many power lists: WSJ Asia's Top Ten Women to Watch in Asia (2006), Fortune India's Most Powerful Women (2011-2018) and Fortune India's Hall of Fame (2013).
deep_cut_fact: She was a Parvin Fellow at Princeton's Woodrow Wilson School of International Affairs. She was also President of the International Union for Housing Finance (IUHF) until 2024.
notes: She is a corporate director, not a founder; her wealth comes from HDFC stock and options. The best route is probably HDFC Bank corporate communications, or the Nudge Life Skills Foundation, where she is a director.

name: Mridu Hari Dalmia
current_role: Former Joint President, OCL India; family-business investor (current directorships unclear; listed by MarketScreener at First Capital India Ltd)
profile: Mridu Hari Dalmia is a son of industrialist Jaidayal Dalmia. With his brothers he controlled OCL India (formerly Orissa Cement), the cement and refractories company, and served as its Joint President. In 2015 he and his family trust sold a combined ~26.6% of OCL to Dalmia Cement (Bharat), a deal worth about US$165m. Hurun lists him as UAE-based.
interesting_fact: OCL changed its name from Orissa Cement Ltd in 1996 to reflect its non-cement ventures. After Jaidayal Dalmia's death it was controlled by his sons Ajay, Mridu and Raghu Hari Dalmia. OCL later became part of Dalmia Bharat.
notes: Very low public profile; I found no interviews, website or social accounts. 'Alive' could not be confirmed from a recent source. His directorships are listed inconsistently across data aggregators, so check MCA filings (DIN 00009529) before approaching. 2015 stake-sale source: https://globalcement.com/news/8916-ocl-india-and-dalmia-bharat-merger-moves-ahead

name: Zou Shenglong
current_role: Founder and Honorary Chairman, Xunlei Limited (Nasdaq: XNET); left the board in Aug 2023
profile: Zou Shenglong (Sean Zou, b. 1973) studied computer science at the University of Wisconsin and earned a Duke master's, then worked in Silicon Valley. He co-founded Xunlei in Shenzhen in 2003 with Cheng Hao, and its P2P download accelerator became one of China's most widely used apps. Xunlei IPO'd on Nasdaq in 2014. He handed the CEO role to Chen Lei in 2017 to focus on AI and life sciences and remains a significant shareholder.
interesting_fact: At the 2014 IPO his wholly owned holding company, Vantage Point Global, was Xunlei's largest shareholder with 27.5%, ahead of VCs Morningside, IDG and Ceyuan.
deep_cut_fact: Xunlei's operating company started life as 'Sandai Technologies (Shenzhen) Inc.' and only took the Xunlei ('thunderbolt') name in May 2005. He met co-founder Cheng Hao while studying at Duke.
notes: Low public profile since 2017; he no longer has an operating role. Xunlei IR is the only published route. The Duke/Cheng Hao detail comes from 36Kr (https://www.36kr.com/p/673038593253379).

name: Cheng Hao
current_role: Founding Partner, iVision Ventures (远望资本), Beijing; co-founder of Xunlei
profile: Cheng Hao co-founded Xunlei with Zou Shenglong in Shenzhen in 2002-03 and led it as CEO through its 2014 Nasdaq IPO. He stepped back from management in January 2016 to invest, and in May 2018 he co-founded iVision Ventures (远望资本) with Silicon Valley friends Tian Hongfei and Jiang Ping. iVision is an AI- and robotics-focused tech VC.
interesting_fact: He says Xunlei's first product was a distributed mailbox, abandoned after about six months before the pivot to downloads. Its P2SP algorithm then made downloads 5 to 10 times faster.
deep_cut_fact: In a 36Kr column he wrote that he once hit the top rank (30 stars) in Honor of Kings in a single season. He also said he learned guitar in college partly to win over a girl.
notes: Active writer and speaker in Chinese tech media (36Kr columns), and iVision has backed robotics companies such as Keenon. The input says 'Hurun Unicorn founders (2026)', but I could not confirm which unicorn; it is likely a portfolio or co-founder link. Approach via iVision Ventures. iVision founding source: https://news.pedaily.cn/201809/436250.shtml

name: Chandra Prakash Madrecha
current_role: Co-founder/director, Trimax IT Infrastructure & Services (Mumbai); listed director of Trimax Data Center Services
profile: Chandra Prakash Madrecha is one of the Udaipur-born Madrecha brothers who founded Trimax IT Infrastructure & Services in Mumbai in 1995. Trimax grew from a hardware assembler into a systems integrator and data-centre/e-governance services firm, best known for electronic ticketing machines for state bus corporations. His brother Surya Prakash was the public face as CMD. Their family also hit the Hurun India list in 2017-18.
interesting_fact: In 2009 Trimax won the open tender to supply electronic ticket-issuing machines to Maharashtra's state bus corporation (MSRTC). It later built similar systems for BEST, Rajasthan, UP and Bangalore transport, and sold ~1.8m BEST smart cards.
deep_cut_fact: The company name Trimax comes from the founders' philosophy of 'try maximum'. The brothers came from a Udaipur family that ran a kirana store and a wholesale sugar business.
notes: Sources disagree on whether Chandra Prakash or his brother Surya Prakash is 'the founder'. Most press covers Surya Prakash, so check before outreach. There is no recent (2024-26) news on Trimax and no published contact. The data-centre background is relevant to the podcast theme.

name: Lisa Ann Basile
current_role: Trustee of The Basile Family Irrevocable Trust; >10% (majority) beneficial owner of JFB Construction Holdings (Nasdaq: JFB)
profile: Lisa Ann Basile is the mother of JFB Construction founder and CEO Joseph F. Basile III. JFB is a Lantana, Florida commercial and residential design-build contractor that listed on Nasdaq in 2025. As trustee of the Basile Family Irrevocable Trust and through her own revocable trust, she reported beneficial ownership of ~65.6% of the Class A stock in a March 2025 Schedule 13D. She holds no operating role.
interesting_fact: Her stake came from her son's April 2024 gift of shares in the JFB operating subsidiary to the family trust she controls, just before the company reorganised for its IPO.

public_contacts.value: CORE IR (JFB investor relations), contact Mike Mason, 516-222-2560

notes: She is a passive holder and a private individual; the business story is her son's (Joseph F. Basile III, CEO). Any outreach should go via JFB/CORE IR and be aimed at the company, not her.

name: Mark Ein
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Venturehouse Group and Capitol Investment Corp; Chairman, Kastle Systems; owner, Washington Kastles & Washington City Paper; Chairman, DC Open
profile: Mark Ein (b. 1964, Chevy Chase MD; Wharton '87, HBS '92) worked at Goldman Sachs, Brentwood Associates and Carlyle before founding Venturehouse Group in 1999. He sponsors the Capitol-series SPACs, which produced public companies such as Custom Truck One Source, Lindblad and Two Harbors, and he chairs Kastle Systems. He is a Washington sports figure: Kastles founder, DC Open chair and a Commanders limited partner.
interesting_fact: He chaired President Biden's President's Export Council from 2023 and was part of Josh Harris's group that bought the Washington Commanders for $6.05bn. He and Harris have been friends since elementary school.
deep_cut_fact: A lifelong tennis player, he played seven or eight pro doubles tournaments in his forties. The Daily Pennsylvanian called him the oldest person ever to receive an ATP doubles ranking. He traces his sports-owner ambitions to hearing 76ers owner Ed Snider speak at Wharton in 1982.
notes: Highly accessible and media-friendly. He owns a newspaper, speaks often at DC business and sports events, and is a WEF contributor. Kastle Systems (building security/access data) is a natural angle for an energy/data-centre podcast. I could not verify a personal X/LinkedIn handle.

name: Chai Guosheng
current_role: Founder and long-time chairman of Guangdong Cnlight Co. (雪莱特光电, SZSE: 002076), Foshan; current role unclear
profile: Chai Guosheng (柴国生, b. 1953) is a lighting engineer who founded Nanhai Huaxing Optoelectronics in 1992. It became Guangdong Cnlight (雪莱特), a maker of energy-saving lamps and light sources that listed in Shenzhen in 2006 with him as controlling shareholder and chairman/president. Filings show his stake fell below 5% by 2023.
interesting_fact: At Cnlight's 2006 IPO he held 66.57% of the company. He was credited with 61 service inventions and a 2004 National Science and Technology Progress Award (second class).
deep_cut_fact: He studied electric light sources in Fudan University's optics department. From 1978 to 1992 he rose from technician to chief engineer at the Gejiu Light Bulb Factory in Yunnan, where in 1986 he co-developed an 'H-type single-ended rare-earth energy-saving fluorescent lamp'.
notes: Low profile and no English-language coverage. His holdings in Cnlight were reduced in 2019-2023 (see SZSE filings), so avoid wealth topics. The best approach is in Chinese via the Cnlight board secretary. His energy-efficient lighting background is relevant to the energy theme.
